reason: This passage (1 Kings 22) explicitly demonstrates and reinforces strict hierarchical structures throughout. Kings command prophets, soldiers, and servants; their orders are carried out (gathering 400 prophets, imprisoning Micaiah); kings wear distinctive royal garments; chariot commanders follow orders; and social rank determines roles and access. Even when Micaiah speaks truth against the king's expectations, he is imprisoned for it—the hierarchy is maintained rather than questioned. The narrative structure itself relies on hierarchical authority relationships being clear and consequential. There is no textual evidence that hierarchy is unimportant or discouraged; rather, it is presented as a fundamental organizing principle.
